content:
Want to use Signal on multiple devices at the same time? This encrypted messaging service is making it easier for users to use the app across multiple iPhones and other devices.

Signal users can now link another iPhone to their existing Signal account, no longer limited to using an iPad as the second mobile device.

Alongside announcing new Android linking capabilities today, the company stated: "We are expanding linked device support on iOS — in addition to the iPad we've always supported, you can now link an iPhone to your Signal account."

When linking an additional iPhone, users can choose whether to transfer their full message history and media files stored within the past 45 days.

Signal said the transfer process uses full end-to-end encryption and the same "link-and-sync" technology used for iPads and desktop devices, including Signal for Mac.

This expanded support is particularly useful for users who need to use two iPhones to separate work and personal matters, or for those who need to test multiple devices.

The move also brings Signal's multi-device experience closer to the Apple Messages ecosystem, allowing users to seamlessly continue conversations across iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Signal for iOS version 8.22 will land on the App Store later. Signal recently also rolled out a username feature, allowing users to make connections without sharing their phone numbers.
